page: Microsoft Azure D96as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, featuring 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 786 GB drive, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core tests placing it in the top 10%. Passmark CPU encryption and image processing benchmarks also reach top-tier levels. Single-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng, though single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing fall into the average category. Memory performance is highly polarized: the Passmark memory score is top-tier, and small-block cached read bandwidth is strong, but large-block uncached read and write bandwidths remain average.

This hardware profile offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense, multi-threaded workloads that benefit from high core counts without requiring specialized GPU acceleration. The instance is well-suited for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, and large-scale web serving. It also supports moderate LLM inference tasks, demonstrating strong text generation speeds for medium-sized models, though performance scales down to average for larger 70B models.
